$comment: Runtime packages a workspace may depend on, each with the reason (CLAUDE.md, Never: a runtime dependency only with an entry here). Every runtime package runs where plain text lives; the client stays at a handful. `bun run lint` fails on a dependency missing here or used by a workspace not listed for it. Workspace packages (@kennwort/*) need no entry.

solid-js.reason: Solid 2, the reactive UI of the web app, the extension and the mobile app (docs/plan.md, Stack); small and auditable instead of React

@solidjs/web.reason: Solid 2's DOM renderer, split out of solid-js in 2.0; the same project and release as solid-js

@tanstack/solid-router.reason: TanStack Router for the web app's addresses and history, code-based routes without codegen (docs/plan.md, Entscheidungen; adopted as a release candidate at the user's request, the first line with Solid 2 support). Its router-core, history, cookie-es and seroval come along; its declared @solidjs/meta, @solid-primitives/refs, @solid-devtools/logger (Solid 1 packages) and isbot are imported by none of the code the web app uses or only by its server rendering, so none of them reaches the shipped bundle (checked with the bundle's source map)

@tanstack/solid-query.reason: TanStack Query for the server data the pages load (devices, groups, members, policy): one in-memory cache per opened account, no persister, keys without secrets (docs/plan.md, Entscheidungen; release candidate with Solid 2 support, adopted at the user's request). Its only dependency is @tanstack/query-core

@noble/ciphers.reason: XChaCha20-Poly1305, and AES-256, ChaCha20 and Salsa20 to read KeePass databases (KDBX 4, import only): audited, pure TypeScript, no dependencies of its own; the only cipher library packages/crypto may use (docs/plan.md, Kryptografie)

@noble/post-quantum.reason: ML-KEM-768 and X-Wing (X25519 + ML-KEM-768, draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem) to wrap keys post-quantum hybrid; audited, pure TypeScript

@noble/hashes.reason: SHA-2, HMAC, HKDF-SHA-512, Argon2id, and Argon2d to read KeePass databases (KDBX 4); audited, pure TypeScript, a dependency of the other @noble packages anyway

@noble/curves.reason: Ed25519 signatures (RFC 8032) and X25519 inside X-Wing; audited, pure TypeScript

zod.reason: Zod 4: every value that crosses between client and server is parsed against a schema (CLAUDE.md, docs/plan.md Stack); no dependencies of its own

hono.reason: the HTTP API of the server (docs/plan.md, Stack): small, standards-based (fetch Request/Response), no dependencies

drizzle-orm.reason: typed SQL and migrations on bun:sqlite for the server (docs/plan.md, Stack); no runtime dependencies of its own

better-auth.reason: sign-in on the server (docs/plan.md, Stack): passkeys, sessions, bearer tokens, rate limits; only on the server, never in a client, and it never decrypts anything (P-02)

@better-auth/passkey.reason: Better Auth's WebAuthn plugin (SimpleWebAuthn) for signing in with a passkey

lucide.reason: the icon data of lucide (DESIGN.md: lucide icons), framework-free arrays without dependencies; lucide-solid needs Solid 1 (splitProps, solid-js/web), so packages/ui renders the arrays itself (docs/plan.md, Entscheidungen)

@fontsource-variable/geist.reason: Geist as a variable font file with its @font-face CSS, shipped with the app instead of loaded from Google Fonts (DESIGN.md, Schrift); no code, only the font and CSS

@fontsource-variable/geist-mono.reason: Geist Mono for passwords, one-time codes and hosts, shipped like Geist (DESIGN.md, Schrift); no code, only the font and CSS

uqr.reason: QR codes on the recovery kit (P-12), for adding a device (P-04) and on the labels for devices and installations (K-605, P-27: the entry's address with IDs only): a dependency-free TypeScript port of Nayuki's reference QR encoder (MIT), generation only; nothing secret beyond what the printed kit shows passes through it

jsqr.reason: reads the QR code a service shows when setting up one-time codes (K-306 part 4b), from the camera or a screenshot; the browsers' BarcodeDetector is missing on desktop Linux and Windows. Pure JavaScript, no dependencies, loaded only when scanning

tldts.reason: the Public Suffix List for the exact host the extension lists and fills by (P-17, K-403): a public suffix such as co.uk or github.io is never taken for one site. Pure functions without I/O or globals; its one dependency is tldts-core from the same project, which has none (pinned with tldts in the root overrides). The list is bundled (about 130 kB minified) into the popup, the inline menu and the service worker, never into the content script. Since K-802 the matcher lives in packages/client (autofill/matches.ts), shared by the extension and the mobile app's autofill, which bundles it into the app's webview build only

tauri.reason: Tauri 3 (3.0.0-alpha.6, the newest; stable is 2.12), the mobile app's shell for Android and iOS (docs/plan.md, Stack; K-801): one system webview on the web app's bundled build, IPC for the autofill plugins of K-802. No feature flags; the Rust side holds no keys and no logic of its own

tauri-runtime-wry.reason: Tauri 3's webview runtime on wry (Android WebView, WKWebView), a separate crate since 3.0 that the app must name; same project and release as tauri

serde.reason: serializes the arguments the Rust command copy_secret hands to the Android clipboard plugin (K-803) and the server bridge's requests and answers (src-tauri/src/bridge.rs); already linked as a dependency of tauri, so the binary gains nothing

serde_json.reason: the JSON value an Android plugin call answers with (PluginHandle::run_mobile_plugin, K-803); already linked as a dependency of tauri, so the binary gains nothing

url.reason: Parses the server address and builds each API address on the one stored origin (src-tauri/src/server.rs); already linked through tauri (it is tauri::Url), named so the rules build and test without the shell

lockedCrates.reason: Every crate apps/mobile/src-tauri/Cargo.lock resolves, direct and indirect (K-802; the gap the review of K-801 left open): the crates of tauri 3.0.0-alpha.6, tauri-runtime-wry, serde, serde_json and url, and their build tools and the desktop backends of `tauri dev` (gtk, webkit2gtk), since Cargo.lock does not mark what only builds or only runs on another target. Checked by name and source (crates.io only) in scripts/allowed-dependencies.ts, lockViolations: a new name fails lint until someone looked at it and added it here; a newer version of a listed crate passes, pinned by Cargo.lock. The crates the app names itself keep their own reasons under crates
